reports.title: Corpay Reports Third Quarter Financial Results

guidance.heading: Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook
section: “We are raising our full-year 2026 outlook to reflect our strong third quarter results and improved expectations for the fourth quarter,” said Peter Walker. “At the midpoint, our updated guidance calls for full-year revenue of $5.35 billion and adjusted net income per diluted share of $28.00, representing growth of 18% and 31%, respectively.”
For fiscal year 2026, Corpay, Inc.'s financial guidance1 is revised as follows:
•Total revenues between $5.340 billion and $5.360 billion, growing 18% at the midpoint year over year;
•Net income per diluted share between $20.03 and $20.23;
•Adjusted net income between $1.847 billion and $1.867 billion; and
•Adjusted net income per diluted share between $27.90 and $28.10, growing 31% at the midpoint year over year.

desk.headline: Revenue up 18% to $1.38bn and adjusted EPS up 32% to $7.54, beat; full-year 2026 outlook raised
results: Revenue grew 18% to $1.38bn; stripping out deals, fuel prices and currency, organic growth was 11%.
Corporate Payments (business cards, supplier payments and cross-border FX) was the engine: revenue +41% as reported and +18% organic, with spend volume up 45% to $95bn.
Vehicle (fuel and toll) payments grew 8% to $580m; lodging payments rose 3% to $131m.
Adjusted EPS rose 32% to $7.54 and GAAP EPS 45% to $5.66, helped by fewer shares.
Bought back 1.9m shares for $747m in the quarter (5.25m for $1.85bn so far this year).

guidance.summary: Full-year 2026 outlook raised for both revenue and adjusted EPS (midpoints $5.35bn and $28.00, growth of 18% and 31%). For Q4 the company expects revenue of about $1.37bn and adjusted EPS of $7.65 at the midpoint.

points: CEO Ron Clarke stressed a sixth straight quarter of double-digit organic growth, with customer retention stable.
Management expects Corporate Payments to keep growing in the high teens; the UK multi-currency account product passed $1bn of annual payment volume.
Recent deals (Alpha and the AvidXchange stake) are said to be beating their earnings targets; non-core businesses are being sold to simplify the group.
About $2bn of yearly free cash flow will go to spend-management acquisitions or buybacks, whichever offers the better return.
The CFO credited high flow-through of extra revenue for a 57.4% EBITDA margin in Corporate Payments.
call.source: Call coverage: StockStory, 5 Nov 2026; CFO comments in the press release

watch: Whether Corporate Payments organic growth holds in the high teens.
Closing of the maintenance business sale and use of proceeds to cut debt.
Fuel prices and FX, which the guidance assumes (US fuel at $4.90 a gallon).
